_comment: One secret-pattern source for Python has_secret and Node containsSecret. Flags are case-insensitive except card/date/url. A card match must stand alone (no letter or digit touching it) and pass the Luhn check, so hex hashes and ids cannot trip it; matches may overlap, and a 16-digit window that follows another digit group ('1234 4111 1111 1111 1111') must also start with a card-network prefix ('card_iin'), have 1 to 4 digit groups before and at most 4 after it in its run with at most 2 of 4+ digits on each side, and is read with every check-digit-valid USPS run removed, so a long grouped order number is not held for its later windows by chance; 'amex' is a 15-digit card starting 34 or 37, compact or written 4-6-5 ('3782 822463 10005') or 4-4-4-3 with one separator, also Luhn-checked; a whole digit run matching 'tracking' (USPS IMpb layout: starts 91-95, groups of 4 then a final 2 for 22 or 26 digits, one space or dash throughout) with a valid GS1 mod-10 check digit is removed before the card check, so a Luhn-passing 16-digit window inside it is not a card. Both sides run them ASCII-only on normalized text (NFKC, casefold, whitespace/control to space, non-ASCII letter to x, digit to 0); Stripe keys have no leading word boundary so a placeholder letter before them cannot hide them. A password/api-key keyword alone is prose; it is held only when a value follows it (after : or = unless the value's first word is a pointer/placeholder (in, see, stored, at, from, none, null, env, vault, keychain, redacted, n/a, tbd, <...>, ${...}), so 'KEY: in other-file.md' is prose; a placeholder is a closed <...>, $(...) or ${...} (at most 200 characters on one line) or, after a plain quote or none, a $NAME, and it must be the WHOLE value: a quote (escaped or not), whitespace, comma, semicolon or end must follow it, so '${VAR}hunter2xyz9' is held; after a backslash-escaped quote (KEY=\"$(...)\" inside a code string) $NAME is not a placeholder, so a literal \"$3cret9\" or an unclosed \"$(Secret9\" is still held - the token rule's key/secret assignments use the same test; or after 'is' when the value has a digit or symbol).
